messages.content:
Follow these writing rules. They matter as much as the content:

- Generator scaffolding left in: oaicite, [cite: 1], placeholders -- finish the text and read it
- The "it's not X, it's Y" construction -- just state Y
- A bolded word opening a list item as a per-item tag -- reserve bold for a rare callout
- Saying "is" the long way: serves as, boasts, functions as -- use the plain verb
- One-line dramatic fragments: "That's it. That's the whole thing." -- cut them, the preceding sentence already made the point
- Em dashes clustering in one document -- most drafts need 0-2; use commas, periods or parentheses for the rest
- Filler verbs: leverages, facilitates, unlocks -- use a plain verb, or cut the sentence
- A snake_case identifier written as plain prose -- name it in words, or mark it as inline code
- Marketing cliches: "hidden gem", "let's dive in" -- say the specific thing
- The "Not X. Not Y." listing construction -- state the point once
- Stock section skeleton: "Despite its success", "Looking ahead" -- name the specific thing the section is for
- Standalone filler adverbs: undoubtedly, arguably, notably, importantly, ultimately -- most add nothing; cut them unless one is carrying real emphasis
- A banned synonym of one of this project's canonical terms, per its declared lexicon -- one word, one meaning: use the canonical term the word's own note names
- Dramatic turning points with nothing concrete behind them: "Everything changed." -- name the actual event, or cut it

Now write the following. Return only the requested text.
Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
Dark mode is here. Open Settings > Appearance and pick Dark, Light, or System, and the app matches your OS automatically if you choose the last one.

We built this because our top feature request for two years was relief from the white glare of the editor at night. The new theme dims the canvas, sidebar, and toolbar together, and we rewrote the syntax highlighting palette so code blocks and markdown symbols stay readable against the darker background instead of washing out.

A few details we cared about while building this. Contrast ratios meet WCAG AA across every text color in the app, including muted metadata like timestamps and tags. Images and embedded PDFs keep their original colors so your reference material doesn't get color-shifted. And the switch is instant: no flash of the old theme while pages reload, no flicker when you jump between notes.

Sync respects your choice per device. If you want dark mode on your laptop at night and light mode on your tablet during the day, set them independently; the app won't overwrite one with the other.

This is the first release of a larger visual overhaul. Next up: custom accent colors and adjustable editor contrast, both currently in testing with a small group of beta users.

If you hit a spot where dark mode looks off, a note background that didn't update or a plugin that clashes with the new palette, tell us through in-app feedback. We're tracking every report and fixing them in order of how many people hit them.

Try it under Settings > Appearance today.
